findings.observed: python app/app.py menu (project root) and python app.py menu (from app/) both output exactly 'sections: home, notes, stats, help' with exit 0; 'archive' is absent. Reproduced identically on a second cycle. open archive itself works and returns '2025 entries' with exit 0.
findings.expected_basis: Public docs app/README.md: 'Documentation portal with five sections: home, notes, stats, archive and help.' and 'python app.py menu lists all sections.' The menu output contradicts both sentences; the original goal frames reachability 'as described in app/README.md'. A first-time user relying on the menu cannot discover archive.
findings.reproduction: 1) cd to project root; 2) run: python app/app.py menu; 3) observe 4-item list lacking 'archive'; 4) run: python app/app.py open archive; 5) observe it succeeds — proving the omission is in the listing, not the section

findings.observed: open notes displays 'milk, eggs' (2 items) while open stats displays '5 notes'. Both outputs are stable across two observation cycles. README documents no pagination or filtering that would reconcile the counts.
findings.expected_basis: Internal state contradiction: the product's own stats section contradicts what its notes section displays to the same user in the same session. At least one of the two surfaces presents wrong information.
findings.reproduction: 1) run: python app/app.py open notes; 2) observe 'milk, eggs'; 3) run: python app/app.py open stats; 4) observe '5 notes'

non_findings_notes: 'open' with no argument and unknown section names return graceful 'unknown section' with exit 0 — no documented expectation contradicted
section names are case-sensitive ('open HOME' → unknown section); README uses lowercase names
--help is rejected (exit 2); --help is not documented, and the usage line instead reveals an undocumented --smoke flag
